milestone: FIRST EXECUTABLE FIXTURES FOR CLAUSE 13. The clause became source-complete at batch139 with 283/283 base units and zero executable tests.

why_this_clause_is_testable.mechanism: Format output is byte-exactly testable through an internal WRITE to a character variable - no files, no I/O units, no scratch directories. That makes these the cleanest oracles in the suite.
why_this_clause_is_testable.the_trap: It is so easy that a vacuous test slips through. Character comparison BLANK-PADS THE SHORTER OPERAND, so comparing a buffer against a shorter literal silently passes. Every output helper therefore asserts LEN before equality, and widths vary so that padding is load-bearing rather than incidental.
why_this_clause_is_testable.why_this_target_first: Integer and BOZ editing involve no reals and no processor-dependent kinds, so the arithmetic is exact and the oracles are unambiguous.

source_rules_independently_confirmed: SS suppresses the optional plus sign; a negative value's minus sign is mandatory
Output is right-justified; w=0 output uses the smallest positive field width
w=0 is PROHIBITED on input (13.7.5.1 p1)
m has no effect on input
Lowercase hex a-f is equivalent to uppercase on input
oracles_hand_derived_and_confirmed: I5 with -42 -> '  -42', safe without SS because the minus is required

non_vacuity_by_descriptor_substitution.principle: Oracle and input mutation alone is PROVABLY INSUFFICIENT - one packet's vacuity survived a 114-mutation campaign and was exposed only by mutating the feature under test. For a DESCRIPTOR packet the decisive mutation is substituting the descriptor, the direct analogue of the operator-substitution sweep that caught batch125 and batch127.
non_vacuity_by_descriptor_substitution.campaign: 102 mutations, all failing on BOTH toolchains: 23 input mutations, every text and integer oracle mutation, 5 SS->SP, reverse sentinel mutations, and 13 descriptor substitutions.
non_vacuity_by_descriptor_substitution.reviewer_reran: ALL THIRTEEN descriptor substitutions on both toolchains; all failed. Required samples I5.4->I5, B4.4->O4.4 and O4.4->Z4.4 all failed on both.
non_vacuity_by_descriptor_substitution.vacuity_check_on_the_substitutions_thems: A substitution is only load-bearing if the two descriptors DIFFER on the chosen value. The integrator raised this explicitly and the reviewer verified it: B4.4(5)=0101 while O/Z give 0005; O4.4(8)=0010 while B gives 1000 and Z gives 0008; Z4.4(10)=000A while B gives 1010 and O gives 0012. No substitution coincides, so none is vacuous.
non_vacuity_by_descriptor_substitution.permanence: The BOZ matrix is permanent in build_boz_output_minimum_m_digits, and the integer descriptor substitutions are generator-owned. A one-off manual check would not have been acceptable.

audits.sign_mode: Every positive-value output case uses SS, so no case depends on the optional plus, which is processor dependent. The single case without SS uses -42, where the minus is mandatory - confirmed safe.
audits.zero_width: No input case uses I0, B0, O0 or Z0, respecting the prohibition on w=0 for input.
audits.len_assertion: All output helpers assert LEN before equality; no oracle can pass by blank-padding a shorter literal.
audits.padding_load_bearing: Widths vary rather than always equalling the digit count.
audits.no_zero_reliance: No observed result relies on the value 0, which would be default-equivalent.

findings.issue: The case also observes leading-zero padding while BOZ-output-leading-zeros-to-m is left pending - that is UNDER-CLAIMING, not vacuity.
findings.action: No correction required for this packet.

compiler_observations.integrator_corroboration: The integrator independently hand-derived and corroborated five oracles - (SS,I5.4) 42, B4.4 5, O4.4 8, Z4.4 10 and O4 8 - against gfortran before dispatching the review. Compiler agreement is corroboration only; every value was derived from the source first.

explicit_limitations: NOT established: the optional plus under S, zero special cases, m>w, enum and enumeration editing, real and complex BOZ representation, unacceptable-field error conditions, list-directed and external I/O, and R1323 syntax coverage. The reviewer confirmed these exclusions are honest and that none is quietly claimed anyway.
Passing under two compilers is corroboration, not proof of universal conformance.
